node.title: Re: read files one by one in directory and redirct output to a file (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
You've commented out a bunch of code, why? It's unclear what problem you're having, and unclear how which code is relevant to the question. Please take the time to read and follow [id://174051] and [id://1177642|SSCCE] - if you follow that advice, we will be able to provide help much more efficiently.

Just a guess, but perhaps [doc://readdir] is returning directories as well as just files? And as [huck] pointed out, the filenames returned by [doc://readdir] don't include the directory name. Here, I'm using catfile from [doc://File::Spec] to prefix the directory name to the filename, no_upwards from the same module to filter directory entries like . (curdir) and .. (parent dir), and [doc://-X|-f] to filter out only files. The [doc://sort] is optional.

use File::Spec::Functions qw/no_upwards catfile/; opendir my $dh, $dirname or die "$dirname: $!"; my @files = grep {-f} map {catfile $dirname, $_} sort +no_upwards readdir $dh; closedir $dh;

Update: Fixed: "sort no_upwards" was not correct, but the -f test was hiding the issue.
